newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oil World cuts Latin American oilseed forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Oil World cuts Latin American oilseed forecasts.

text.p: Argentina's soybean crop is forecast at 12.7 million tonnes, compared with the 13.0 million forecast on March 25 and last year's harvest of 12.5 million, the independent Oil World newsletter said.
It cited the impact of drought, adding that Oil World sources saw further downward potential of between 400,000 and 600,000 tonnes.
Oil World also lowered its forecast for this year's Argentine sunseed crop to 4.9 million from 5.6 million last year and the 5.2 million forecast two weeks ago.
This implied sunseed yields of 1.65 tonnes per hectare, a four-year low.
Oil World also said it had lowered its forecast for Brazil's 1997 soybean crop to 26.9 million tonnes from 27.2 million previously.
Citing dry weather in some regions, it said the crop would still be sharply up on the 23.9 million produced in 1996.
Brazilian farmers were actively selling soybeans and products at current high prices for shipment up to August, ahead of a probably ample U.S. crop.
